SITUATION
A industrial fermentation plant running a batch ethanol fermentation has seen fermentation yield fall about 25% over the past three weeks, repeating batch after batch. The drop began after a cleaning-protocol change and a switch to a new yeast-propagation batch. The production team's leading theories are that fermentation runs too cool or is underfed, so they favor warmer temperatures and more sugar feed. Batches have smelled faintly sour at the end of fermentation. Routine process panels read broadly within range. The feed, temperature, dosing, and treatment systems are all adjustable, and dosing and treatment options are available. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available controls or additives, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: EthanolYield (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)
MEASURABLE SIGNALS (ids):
  m0: organic-acid titer
  m1: carbonation level
  m2: nitrogen source
  m3: inoculation volume
  m4: ethanol yield
  m5: original gravity
  m6: clarifier dose
  m7: co2 offgas rate
  m8: agitation rate
  m9: dissolved oxygen
  m10: vessel pressure
  m11: sugar feed rate
  m12: yeast generation

CONTROLS (ids):
  a0: set carbonation level range [0, 100]
  a1: sugar feed rate range [0, 100]

  a3: set inoculation volume range [0, 100]

  a5: set original gravity range [0, 100]
  a6: set nitrogen source range [0, 100]
  a7: set clarifier dose range [0, 100]
  a8: set agitation rate range [0, 100]

(none yet)
